rules.statement: When an operation must be applied to every item in a collection that matches a condition, process all matches and return only after the loop, rather than returning after the first match.
rules.why: An early return inside the loop leaves later matching items unprocessed, so the gap the change meant to close stays open and the run reports success without warning.
rules.check: Look for `return` (or `break`) inside a loop that applies a fix or setting to matching items, where the intent is to cover all matches; check that a test with two or more matching items verifies each one is handled.

rules.statement: When updating an existing external resource whose expected sub-object is missing, report it and leave it unchanged instead of writing invented default values for its other fields.
rules.why: Writing made-up defaults would silently change settings the owner chose, such as review counts or allowed merge methods, on a resource the code does not own.
rules.check: Look for fallback branches that build a full parameter set from literals when the fetched object lacks one, then send it in an update; it should skip and report instead, with a test covering the missing-field case.

rules.statement: Define a set of configuration values once and reuse it, rather than repeating the same literals in more than one code path.
rules.why: Duplicated literal sets can drift apart when the settings change, and nothing flags the drift.
rules.check: Look for the same group of parameter literals (e.g. a settings object or request body) written out in two places in the diff.

rules.statement: When a change alters user-visible behavior, update every documentation passage that describes the old behavior so the docs don't contradict each other.
rules.why: Stale passages give readers two contradicting accounts of what the tool does.
rules.check: For a behavior change in the diff, search usage docs and READMEs for wording that still describes the previous behavior.

rules.statement: Before flagging a changelog entry as misplaced or stray, check how earlier release sections place the same kind of entry, and don't report it when it follows that existing pattern.
rules.why: The maintainer kept a test-only 'no change for projects' note as the last bullet under Changed because earlier sections put the same kind of note in the same place.
rules.check: Compare the entry's position and kind with earlier sections of the same CHANGELOG before reporting it.

rules.statement: In test code, cover each call site of a shared helper with at least one case that reaches it through that call site's own conditions, not only through other paths that happen to call the same helper.
rules.why: If a call site is reached only incidentally, a regression there fails no test.
rules.check: For a helper called from several branches, check that the tests include fixtures that reach each branch, e.g. inputs that don't match the special-cased names.
